A '''think tank''' is a gathering of domain experts.

== Aim ==

Common stated goals of think tanks include:

* Facilitate collective reflection and formulating of new ideas
* Elaborate and publish results for the public and policy makers

<ref>{{#cite:Q2650}}</ref>
== Organisation ==

A think tank can be organised as

* a non-profit organisation
* an academic institution, sometimes as part of a larger academic institution (e.g., universities)
* an informal gathering with no judicial entity
* corporation or governmental agency (more controversial)

<ref>{{#cite:Q2650}}</ref>
== Funding ==

Primary sources of funding of a think tank may include:

* private donations
* institutional funding (e.g., when a think tank is part of a university)
* government subsidy, when the work of a think tank informs public policy
* private funding, when the work of a think tank can be of commercial interest

<ref>{{#cite:Q2650}}</ref>
== Desired quality ==

A think tank of public interest is expected to

* be open to different ideas and promote independent thinking
* not be influenced by special interest groups
* publish their work in accessible formats

<ref>{{#cite:Q2650}}</ref>
